newsitem.title: GREECE: CONSTRUCTION CONTINUES TO PULL GREEK STOCKS HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: CONSTRUCTION CONTINUES TO PULL GREEK STOCKS HIGHER.

text.p: Greek shares were 0.26 percent firmer in early Thursday trade, carrying the tone from Wednesday's strong show with construction again setting the pace.

"Construction stocks returned to the limelight very aggressively after spending a long time in the shadow because the market was disappointed by poor performance in the sector's second-liners," said Vasilis Kavvalos, analyst at Omega Securities.
"Investors jumped in as soon as constructions started to play up, recovering from a long period of price weakness," he added.
From a technical point of view, the benchmark index was expected to test critical resistance points in the near-term.
"There is room for further appreciation before the index tests the 1,630 and 1,660 resistance levels," said Kavvalos.
"Should the index break higher than 1,660 points on strong turnover, that level may well become the base for the next leg of a rally in prices, forming a long-term upward channel."
July CPI inflation eased to 5.4 percent from June's 5.5 percent.

"Although July's inflation rate was fully in line with expectations, it gave a positive note on trading because it signalled the return to a downtrend in inflation which will take us closer to 5.0 percent in the coming months," he said.
"But I do not expect any improvement in interest rates over the same period, given the government's heavy fiscal needs," he added.
The Athens general index was up 0.26 percent or 4.17 points at 1,615.63 from Wednesday's 1,611.46 after 25 minutes of trading.
Turnover was 2.0 billion drachmas on volume of 0.6 million shares, helped by a large block trade in Attica Enterprises.
Advancers were leading decliners 91 to 34 with 17 shares unchanged on 142 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.3-$10.8. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,120-1,150 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,046-1,106 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock was up 5 drachmas at 6,300.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 655.30-697.12 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $71.83-$74.60. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,554-3,777 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.03 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 235-267 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
